title: Washington, D.C. Trivia Challenge
intro: One fascinating question at a time. See how much you know and discover the story behind each answer.

questions.question: What material is the U.S. Capitol's famous dome primarily made from?
questions.explanation: Although it resembles stone, the dome is constructed from cast iron and was completed in 1866.

questions.question: What is the name of the statue standing atop the Capitol dome?
questions.explanation: The 19½-foot bronze Statue of Freedom stands above the Capitol.

questions.question: How tall is the Statue of Freedom itself, without its pedestal?
questions.explanation: The Architect of the Capitol lists the bronze statue itself at 19 feet 6 inches; the pedestal adds another 18½ feet.

questions.question: When was the Capitol's current iron dome finished?
questions.explanation: The dome was begun in September 1855 and finished in January 1866, despite the Civil War.

questions.question: About how many pounds of ironwork make up the Capitol dome?
questions.explanation: The Capitol Visitor Center gives a figure of 8,909,200 pounds of ironwork.

questions.question: What unusual metal caps the very top of the Washington Monument?
questions.explanation: An 8.9-inch aluminum tip was placed atop the capstone in 1884, when aluminum was still costly and difficult to refine.

questions.question: About how tall is the Washington Monument?
questions.explanation: The NPS measures its height at 555 feet, 5⅛ inches.

questions.question: Why can you see different shades of stone on the Washington Monument?
options: Two major construction phases using different marble
questions.explanation: Construction stopped in the 1850s and resumed later with marble from a different quarry; the stone weathered differently.

questions.question: What do the Latin words 'Laus Deo' on the monument's aluminum cap mean?
questions.explanation: The National Park Service identifies the inscription as 'Laus Deo,' or 'Praise be to God.'

questions.question: How many exterior Doric columns circle the Lincoln Memorial?
questions.explanation: The 36 columns represent the states in the Union when Abraham Lincoln died.

questions.question: In how many pieces was Lincoln's marble statue carved?
questions.explanation: The Piccirilli brothers carved the massive figure from 28 blocks of Georgia marble.

questions.question: There are 87 steps from the Reflecting Pool to the Lincoln Memorial chamber. Was that number deliberately chosen to echo 'four score and seven'?
options: Yes, the architect wrote that it was
No, the NPS says it appears coincidental
questions.explanation: The NPS says 87 steps is a coincidence; there is no supporting evidence in the architect's plans that the number was intentionally symbolic.

questions.question: Which singer gave an open-air concert at the Lincoln Memorial in 1939?
questions.explanation: Marian Anderson gave a landmark open-air concert on the memorial's steps in 1939.

questions.question: How many gold stars appear on the World War II Memorial's Freedom Wall?
questions.explanation: Each of the 4,048 gold stars represents approximately 100 Americans who died in the war.

questions.question: How many granite columns form the ring around the World War II Memorial?
questions.explanation: Fifty-six columns represent the states and U.S. jurisdictions represented in the war years.

questions.question: What small wartime phrase is engraved twice at the World War II Memorial?
questions.explanation: Two 'Kilroy Was Here' engravings are tucked into corners of the memorial.

questions.question: How many stainless-steel soldier statues stand at the Korean War Veterans Memorial?
questions.explanation: The 19 statues reflect in a dark polished wall to create the effect of 38 figures.

questions.question: Why are the 19 Korean War statues positioned beside a reflective wall?
options: To double their apparent number to 38
questions.explanation: Their reflection makes 38 figures, a reference to the 38th parallel.

questions.question: How are names organized on the Vietnam Veterans Memorial Wall?
questions.explanation: Names are arranged by date of casualty, beginning at the center and ultimately returning there.

questions.question: How old was Maya Lin when her design was chosen for the Vietnam Veterans Memorial?
questions.explanation: Maya Lin was a 21-year-old Yale architecture student when her design won the national competition in 1981.

questions.question: What was the original statue inside the Jefferson Memorial made of?
questions.explanation: The original figure was plaster because wartime restrictions affected metal. A bronze statue replaced it in 1947.

questions.question: How tall is the bronze Thomas Jefferson statue in the Jefferson Memorial?
questions.explanation: The NPS describes the bronze statue as 19 feet tall.

questions.question: Since which year has the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier been guarded continuously, day and night?
questions.explanation: Guards were first assigned during daylight hours in 1926; continuous 24-hour guarding began in 1937.

questions.question: How many steps does a Tomb Guard take on each length of the ceremonial mat?
questions.explanation: The sentinel takes 21 steps and pauses for 21 seconds at points in the ritual.

questions.question: During November, how often is the public Changing of the Guard ceremony held at Arlington?
questions.explanation: From October 1 through March 31, the ceremony is scheduled every hour on the hour.

questions.question: Who lit the eternal flame at President John F. Kennedy's gravesite?
questions.explanation: Arlington's official account says Mrs. Kennedy lit the eternal flame.

questions.question: What year was the current Washington family tomb at Mount Vernon opened?
questions.explanation: The New Tomb opened in 1831 and became the final resting place of George and Martha Washington.

questions.question: Which crop did George Washington begin emphasizing instead of tobacco in the 1760s?
questions.explanation: Mount Vernon's biography notes Washington switched from tobacco to wheat as his main cash crop in the 1760s.
